newsitem.title: USA: Brent sellers flirt with U.S. Gulf Coast refiners.
newsitem.headline: Brent sellers flirt with U.S. Gulf Coast refiners.

text.p: Brent sellers continue to flirt with U.S. Gulf Coast refiners but firm offers remain elusive in a market already saturated with crude, trade sources said on Wednesday.

The May spread between bellwethers West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent was around $1.30-40 a barrel Wednesday afternoon, a level that some consider borderline in transatlantic economics.
But amid languishing demand in Europe, sellers have been probing interest among Gulf Coast buyers.
Brent was assessed around May WTI minus 80-90 cents a barrel for end-April arrival.
One Texas buyer was skeptical about the sellers' intentions. "Nobody's serious," he said, despite a flurry of phone calls.
Buyers were scratching their heads over which companies actually hold Brent cargoes, he added.
"The big game is find out who has the Brents," he said. "It's like a shell game."
Swiss-based trader Glencore has already fixed a vessel, traders said, but it's still not clear whether it's headed to the Gulf Coast or South Africa.
"They're going back and forth between South Africa and the Gulf Coast. No one really knows yet," one trader said.
Among Norwegian crudes, Statoil is showing a Gullfaks cargo for end-April arrival at around May WTI minus $1.00 a barrel, traders said.
West African crude remains abundant, with Nigerian Forcadoes pegged at May WTI minus 60 cents a barrel, and Qua Iboe around minus 10 cents.
Demand is expected to pick in May in anticipation of the summer driving season, but refiners are taking their time for the moment.
"Everybody's looking and shopping," one Gulf Coast buyer said. "I think people are looking for bargains."
Latin American activity remains muted in the week before Easter.
Several Latin countries begin their Easter holidays tomorrow and return to work next week.
The NYMEX and IPE are closed on Friday to observe Good Friday. The IPE is also closed Easter Monday, March 31.
